# Sarath Sundar Harisaravanan: all facts

> The complete set of facts used by the AI chat on https://saraths-portfolio.vercel.app. Each section is one fact, with the homepage section it appears in.

Keep team credit and award wording exactly as written below. Numbers are as stated by Sarath and are not independently benchmarked unless noted.

## About Sarath

Sarath Sundar Harisaravanan is an MS Computer Science student at the University of Southern California (USC) in Los Angeles, expected to graduate in May 2028. He has more than two years of full-time backend and AI software work at IDFC FIRST Bank in Bangalore, India, preceded by an internship there. He builds useful software around real business workflows, works across backend systems and applied AI, and likes turning unfamiliar problems into working tools. Most recently he built Drigil with a three-person team, earning 2nd place in Anthropic's Claude for Public Benefit track at Cal Hacks 13.0.

Source: https://saraths-portfolio.vercel.app/#about

## IDFC · Go MCP server

At IDFC FIRST Bank, Sarath built a Go MCP (Model Context Protocol) server with the engineering team. It exposed enterprise capabilities as tools AI agents could call, across banking domains including CRM, asset management, gold loans, property loans and charge waivers. The team chose a shared tool layer over per-agent API integrations for typed schemas, centralized authentication and reuse across agents, accepting the cost of an extra network hop and another service to maintain. It cut CRM and asset-management lookups from minutes to under 5 seconds. Specific auth protocols, schema libraries or hosting details are not in these notes.

Source: https://saraths-portfolio.vercel.app/#x-mcp

Source: https://saraths-portfolio.vercel.app/#x-idfc

## Drigil · overview

Drigil won 2nd place in Anthropic's Claude for Public Benefit track at Cal Hacks 13.0 (October 2026). It is a track placement, not an overall hackathon placement. Built over 36 hours at the Palace of Fine Arts in San Francisco by a three-person team: Sarath Sundar Harisaravanan, Shraddha Khanapur and Michael Kim. Drigil uses smart glasses to coach people with intellectual and developmental disabilities through a new job, in their supervisor's own voice. It is a hackathon prototype; no clinical study or measured user outcomes are recorded. Which components Sarath personally built is not recorded; it is a team project.

Source: https://saraths-portfolio.vercel.app/#p-drigil · https://devpost.com/software/drigil

## Drigil · how it works

Drigil has three loops. Teach once: a supervisor narrates one demonstration; Drigil picks keyframes where the hands pause, aligns them with a word-level transcript from Cartesia ink-whisper, and Claude turns them into a structured task specification. Coach live: Claude runs confidence-gated vision checks on the camera feed, coaching plays in a cloned supervisor voice through Cartesia with audio cached per line, and a mastery model reduces prompting as the worker gets up to speed. Fix what breaks: if a step keeps causing difficulty, Factory Droid starts a sandboxed agent that rewrites that step; the supervisor reviews a before-and-after comparison and must approve it before it goes live. Stack: Claude, Cartesia, SpacetimeDB, Moss, Factory Droid, Notability.

Source: https://saraths-portfolio.vercel.app/#p-drigil · https://devpost.com/software/drigil

## RegLens

RegLens (2026 to present) is an AI policy-review platform in Python with LangGraph, LangChain, pgvector and PostgreSQL. It checks internal policies against regulatory requirements, retrieves evidence from 25,000+ documents and flags gaps with citations, routing remediation through human approval. It orchestrates four LangGraph agents and has a 500+ query evaluation harness measuring 92% recall@5 and 96% citation accuracy. Integration with Palantir Foundry and AIP ontology modeling is in progress, not finished. There is no public repository.

Source: https://saraths-portfolio.vercel.app/#p-reglens

## NFTGenesis · IEEE paper

NFTGenesis (September 2024) is an image generation and authentication platform built by a four-person team in Python with PyTorch, Stable Diffusion, QLoRA and CNNs. Fine-tuning Stable Diffusion with QLoRA reduced trainable parameters by over 90%. Paired encoder and decoder CNNs embed tamper-evident image signatures with 98% verification accuracy. Sarath authored the paper with the team: "NFTGenesis: An NFT Generation and Authentication System with Market Intelligence Using Deep Learning Based Steganography", IEEE InC4 2024.

Source: https://saraths-portfolio.vercel.app/#p-nft · https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10649392

## Yet Another Kafka

Yet Another Kafka (2023) is a distributed publish-subscribe message broker Sarath built in Java with raw TCP sockets and multithreading, without external frameworks. By his account it handled 20+ topics, 80+ partitions with persistent offset tracking, 250+ concurrent clients, 35,000+ messages per second and sub-50 ms p95 latency; he profiled and debugged bottlenecks along the way. Durability guarantees, replication and benchmark hardware are not described in these notes.

Source: https://saraths-portfolio.vercel.app/#p-kafka · https://github.com/sarathsundarh/BD_yetanother_kafka

## Mend · USC Origin finalist

Mend was a finalist (Top 15 teams) at the USC Origin Hackathon 2026, built by a five-person team: Sarath Sundar Harisaravanan, Anshuman Shrivastav, Dongyeop Lee, Srinivas Patnaik Balivada and Pablo Valdes. It turns one photo of street damage into a verified repair report: an iOS app (SwiftUI) with on-device damage models, server-side vision verification and a city work-queue dashboard on Supabase. Sarath built the pricing and rewards engine: surge pricing over H3 hexagons (about a city block each) where a live 1x to 5x multiplier rises where coverage is thin or stale and cools as reports pile up; one shared module prices both the map and the payout, and each report is priced before it is saved. He also wrote the reward rate card (severity x asset tier x first finder x zone, with a daily cap), itemized receipts, bounty budgets and pay-per-visit sponsored campaigns with geofenced check-ins, covered by 11 Deno unit tests and 39 end-to-end database checks. Teammates built the iOS app, the damage models and the verification flow.

Source: https://saraths-portfolio.vercel.app/#p-mend · https://devpost.com/software/mend-do4rht

## Caldera

Caldera (June 2025) is a full-stack spend-management app in TypeScript, Next.js, React, PostgreSQL and Tailwind CSS, with transaction entry, categorization, search and filtering, type-safe APIs and reusable dashboards. It has 35+ automated tests, and load tests showed a 65% reduction in p95 latency to under 250 ms. It is not shown on this page.

Source: https://saraths-portfolio.vercel.app/#projects

## Data science projects

NIFTY 50 forecasting: an LSTM forecasting prototype in Python with TensorFlow/Keras on minute-level market data, with sliding-window sequences, a chronological split, prediction plots and recursive multi-step forecasts. It is a prototype, not validated backtesting or a trading result. Exoplanet habitability classification (2023): exploratory analysis and a comparison of Logistic Regression and Balanced Random Forest under severe class imbalance, using confusion matrices to weigh false positives against false negatives. Neither project has headline accuracy numbers to quote.

Source: https://saraths-portfolio.vercel.app/#projects · https://github.com/sarathsundarh/nifty50_pred

## How Sarath builds with AI agents

Sarath uses AI-assisted development. After an Anthropic multi-agent workshop he described his approach: a read-only critic agent that reviews changes, shared rules in a CLAUDE.md file, and fewer agents with clearer briefs and deadlines, which he found led to fewer broken handoffs and less rework. No measured speedup is recorded.

Source: https://saraths-portfolio.vercel.app/#notes

## How this chat works

AI Sarath is this chat. It answers only from a curated knowledge base of Sarath's resume facts, retrieved with BM25, using a Gemini model on a Vercel serverless function. Every answer cites its sources, the page can scroll to and circle what it cites, inputs are length-limited and rate-limited, and it says so when it doesn't know something.

Source: https://saraths-portfolio.vercel.app/#notes
